description: SofaBuffers wire-format test vectors generated from the C encoder. Each vector lists the message structure (ordered encode operations and their values) and the exact bytes the encoder produced.

notes.serialized.hex: lowercase hex of the full (dense) message; primitive-layer ground truth and the decoder's skip input
notes.serialized_sparse.hex: lowercase hex of the sparse-canonical message (MESSAGE_SPEC S2): every leaf field equal to its type default is omitted, and a sequence left without content is omitted too (not framed empty); byte-exact target for a sparse encoder
notes.field.element: true marks the op at a wrapper array's LAST element index (MESSAGE_SPEC S2/S5.1). A wrapper carries no length, so the length is highest present id + 1: that element is ALWAYS written -- a leaf as its (default) value, a sequence element as an empty frame -- while every INTERIOR element equal to its default is omitted, leaf and sequence element alike. It is the only op the sparse column never drops
notes.integers: decimal JSON number literals (full u64/i64 range)
notes.floats: finite values as JSON numbers; +/-infinity as the strings 'inf'/'-inf'
notes.blob.value_hex: lowercase hex of the blob payload
notes.array.element_type: input element width/type fed to the encoder (u8..u64, i8..i64, fp32, fp64)
notes.invalid_utf8: NEGATIVE vectors: a `string` field (id 0) whose bytes are not valid UTF-8. A strict (SOFAB_STRICT_UTF8) build MUST decode serialized_hex to the INVALID outcome and refuse to encode string_hex with the invalid-argument error. Backward-compatible: consumers that only read 'vectors' ignore this key. See test_vectors_README.md.
notes.sequence_growth: GROWTH cases (CORELIB_PLAN S7.2 item 8): a wrapper array's length is highest present id + 1 (MESSAGE_SPEC S5.1), so its container grows as elements arrive -- the one allocation shape where growth is conformant (ARCHITECTURE S9.5). A case is keyed by a DELIVERY SEQUENCE OF ELEMENT IDS, not by bytes, because two ports that grow differently emit identical bytes: the port builds the message from 'deliver' and asserts 'expect'. Indices are CAP-RELATIVE -- 'id_from_cap'/'length_from_cap' are offsets added to the port's own configured max_dyn_array_count, which is per-target and never a family-wide number; every case assumes a cap of at least 4. Gated by requires 'dynamic_arrays': statically bounded profiles (C, C++ corelib: c-cpp, Rust no_std) never grow and do not run this block. Expectations come from ARCHITECTURE S9.5 and CORELIB_PLAN S7.2 item 8, NOT from the generating implementation, which authors these cases without executing them. Backward-compatible: consumers that only read 'vectors' ignore this key. See test_vectors_README.md.

vectors.name: skip_long_int_arrays

vectors.name: skip_large_id

vectors.name: skip_at_message_edges

vectors.name: skip_fixlen_at_message_end
vectors.description: A fixlen field is the last thing in the message and is skipped: the decoder must leave the payload state and reach the message boundary (S4.6, S5.2).

vectors.name: skip_int_array_at_message_end
vectors.description: An integer array is the last thing in the message and is skipped: the element loop must run out exactly at the boundary (S4.7, S5.2).

vectors.name: skip_fixlen_array_at_message_end
vectors.description: A fixlen array is the last thing in the message and is skipped: count x element_length must run out exactly at the boundary (S4.8, S5.2).

vectors.name: skip_sequence_at_message_end
vectors.description: A nested sequence is the last thing in the message and is skipped: skip_depth must unwind to zero on the closing marker, or the message never reaches a boundary (S4.9).

vectors.name: skip_before_sequence_end
vectors.description: The last field inside a sequence the receiver DOES read is skipped, so the resync lands on the sequence-end marker rather than on a value-bearing header (S4.9).

vectors.name: array_string_gap
vectors.description: Array of string with a default (empty) element in the middle: sparse omits id 1, leaving a gap the decoder restores.

vectors.name: array_string_trailing_default
vectors.description: Array of string whose LAST element is the default (empty): it is written anyway, so ["a",""] stays distinct from ["a"] -- the sparse form equals the dense one.

vectors.name: array_string_all_default
vectors.description: Array of only default (empty) string elements: the interior one drops, so it encodes as its final element alone, at id 1 -- not as the empty array.

vectors.name: array_struct_interior_default_element
vectors.description: Array of struct where the middle element holds only a default-valued leaf: sparse drops the element entirely (id gap), and the array still decodes at length 3 from id 2.

vectors.name: array_struct_all_default_elements
vectors.description: Array of two all-default structs: the interior element drops and the last one keeps its empty frame, so [{},{}] stays distinguishable from [] at length 2.

vectors.name: array_of_string_arrays
vectors.description: Array of string arrays: the second row is empty and, being the last element, keeps its frame, so the outer array decodes at length 2.

vectors.name: array_string_leading_default
vectors.description: Array of string with leading and trailing default elements: the leading one leaves an id gap, the trailing one is the last element and is written.

vectors.name: array_element_wire_type_mismatch
vectors.description: Wrapper array whose element id 0 arrives as a SCALAR where the schema declares a sequence (struct) element. MESSAGE_SPEC S7.3: it MUST be skipped exactly as a field with an unknown id is skipped, so it does NOT occupy its id and does NOT count toward the array's length (S5.1) -- a schema-aware receiver reconstructs the slot from the element default, decodes the EMPTY array, and re-encodes these bytes as nothing at all (S2). Control: array_element_empty_frame_present.

vectors.name: array_element_empty_frame_present
vectors.description: The control for array_element_wire_type_mismatch: element id 0 arrives as a well-typed but EMPTY frame. An empty element is a PRESENT element -- it counts toward the length (MESSAGE_SPEC S5.1), so the array decodes at length 1 and keeps the frame on re-encode. Only a wire-type-mismatched element (S7.3) stops counting; the two cases are not the same.

Every skipped field is followed by an unsigned anchor that must still decode with its exact value -- a skip consuming one byte too few or too many is caught there (MESSAGE_SPEC S7.3, S4.3).

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_overlong_c0_80
invalid_utf8.description: Overlong 2-byte NUL (C0 80, Java "Modified UTF-8"): U+0000 must be a single 00 byte.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_overlong_c1
invalid_utf8.description: Overlong 2-byte sequence C1 BF (would decode to U+007F, which is 1-byte ASCII).

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_overlong_3byte
invalid_utf8.description: Overlong 3-byte sequence E0 80 80 (would decode to U+0000).

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_overlong_4byte
invalid_utf8.description: Overlong 4-byte sequence F0 80 80 80 (would decode to U+0000).

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_surrogate_d800
invalid_utf8.description: Lone UTF-16 surrogate code point U+D800 (ED A0 80): never valid in UTF-8.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_surrogate_dfff
invalid_utf8.description: Lone UTF-16 surrogate code point U+DFFF (ED BF BF): never valid in UTF-8.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_out_of_range
invalid_utf8.description: Code point above U+10FFFF (F4 90 80 80 = U+110000): out of the Unicode range.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_bare_continuation
invalid_utf8.description: Bare continuation byte 0x80 with no lead byte.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_lone_ff
invalid_utf8.description: 0xFF: never a valid UTF-8 byte in any position.

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_truncated_2byte
invalid_utf8.description: 2-byte lead C2 with no continuation byte (truncated at end-of-payload -> INVALID).

invalid_utf8.name: utf8_truncated_3byte
invalid_utf8.description: 3-byte lead E2 82 missing its final continuation byte (truncated at end-of-payload).

sequence_growth.name: growth_index_at_cap_minus_one
sequence_growth.description: Two string elements, at id 0 and at the last legal index (cap-1). The array is cap long although two elements arrived: a sparse array allocates by its highest id, not by how many elements were delivered. The at-cap-1 index is accepted (ARCHITECTURE S9.5).

sequence_growth.name: growth_index_at_cap
sequence_growth.description: A string element at id 0, then one at the cap itself. max_dyn_array_count binds the element INDEX for a wrapper array (there is no count header to bind), so id >= cap is LimitExceeded -- checked BEFORE the container grows, so nothing is allocated for it. A policy rejection, not INVALID: the bytes are well-formed and decode under a looser cap (CORELIB_PLAN S6.2.1).

sequence_growth.name: growth_gap_filled
sequence_growth.description: String elements at ids 0, 2 and 3 -- id 1 is an interior element equal to its default and so MUST NOT be written (MESSAGE_SPEC S5.1). The gap is well-formed: the array is 4 long, id 1 holds the element default, and the gap neither shortens nor shifts the array.

sequence_growth.name: growth_no_partial_extension
sequence_growth.description: A string element at id 0, then one at the cap (rejected), then one at id 1. The rejection is terminal (CORELIB_PLAN S6.3), and the container must not be left extended toward the rejected index: the check runs before the grow, so the length never passes what legitimately arrived.

sequence_growth.name: growth_empty_array
sequence_growth.description: A wrapper array framed empty -- the explicit-empty form, with no element at all. There is no highest present id, so the length is 0 and the container never grows (MESSAGE_SPEC S5.1). The zero end of the range the cap bounds at the other.

sequence_growth.name: growth_single_at_cap_minus_one
sequence_growth.description: One string element, at cap-1, with nothing before it. The array is still cap long: the length is highest present id + 1 whatever the delivery order or count, so a single element at the boundary is the whole allocation on its own.

sequence_growth.name: growth_index_at_cap_minus_one_struct
sequence_growth.description: growth_index_at_cap_minus_one with STRUCT elements: each element is a framed sub-sequence carrying one unsigned field at id 0, not a leaf. A framed element reaches the container through the collector's sequence path rather than its leaf path, so the boundary is asserted on both. The verdict is the same -- the bound is the index, never the element kind.

sequence_growth.name: growth_index_at_cap_struct
sequence_growth.description: growth_index_at_cap with STRUCT elements: an over-cap index is LimitExceeded on the framed element path too, before the frame is applied and before the container grows.
